display.title: The Four Chochmos, Part 4 (Chanukah)
display.summary_short: Chanukah gelt is for giving more tzedakah; then the last two chochmos save Reb Yankel from a murder charge and keep Rabbi Yehuda calm at home, where a surprise awaits.
display.summary_long: The storyteller passes on the Rebbe's wish that children know Chanukah gelt is meant for giving more tzedakah. The tenth given to tzedakah was never really ours; Hashem made rich and poor so that people can do kindness, and tzedakah is the one mitzvah where Hashem says, 'Test Me.' In the story, the friends stop at an inn. When a galach is given the spare bed, Rabbi Yehuda leaves, but Reb Yankel is too tired to move. Watching from a tree, Rabbi Yehuda sees the chief galach climb in at midnight, kill the sleeping galach and leave the knife on Reb Yankel's bed. In the struggle that follows, the chief galach loses his little finger, which Rabbi Yehuda wraps in the cloth that once held his four coins. In court he defends his friend; the finger fits, the chief galach confesses, and a grateful Reb Yankel gives him half his wagons. Arriving home, Rabbi Yehuda sees strangers in his house and almost loses his temper, but remembers the fourth chochmah and waits: they are talmidei chachamim staying in his guest room. Four gold coins and a note fall out of the challah, revealing who Avram and Sarah really were, and he builds a guest house.
display.lesson: Give tzedakah generously because it was never really ours, follow a tzaddik's advice, and hold back anger; Hashem rewards hachnasas orchim many times over.
